intro: New this issue: Claude Managed Agents dynamic workflows in public beta, Claude Code Projects open to everyone, Codex composer predictions and a new Windows sandbox, and follow-up questions in Cursor /visualize. From the community, Sentry and Heptabase shipped official Claude plugins, and Autoharness lets Claude Code write its own skills. Before installing third-party plugins, we still suggest scanning them with NVIDIA SkillSpector first.

items.name: Managed Agents dynamic workflows (public beta)
items.summary: A lead agent writes a phased plan, hands it to up to 1,000 sub-agents running in parallel, then merges the results. Good for large code migrations, research and data processing.
items.howTo: In Managed Agents, set multiagent.type to multiagent_20261001, turn on workflows, and add the beta header as the docs describe.
items.accessNote: Requires a Claude API account, which can't be registered directly from mainland China.

items.name: Claude Code Projects open to all Pro/Max users
items.summary: Every Pro and Max user on the Claude Code Projects waitlist has been let in, and there's an official 4-minute getting-started video.
items.howTo: Sign in to Claude Code with a Pro or Max account; start with the intro video in the official post.
items.accessNote: Anthropic doesn't serve mainland China; you need an overseas account and network.

items.name: Claude Dashboards / Claude Motion (beta)
items.summary: Have Claude connect to your data sources and build live dashboards that refresh on their own, or turn a report into an editable animated explainer and export it as MP4.
items.howTo: Just tell Claude “make this data into a dashboard” or “turn this into an animated explainer”. Dashboards need a paid plan; Motion needs Team/Enterprise.
items.accessNote: Needs an overseas paid Claude account and network.

items.name: Sentry's official Claude Code plugin (sentry-mcp)
items.summary: Once installed it starts a tuned Sentry sub-agent, so you can look up errors, read stack traces and pin down issues right inside Claude Code.
items.howTo: claude plugin marketplace add getsentry/sentry-mcp, then claude plugin install sentry-mcp@sentry-mcp.
items.accessNote: GitHub usually opens and downloads fine from mainland China; using it with Claude Code needs an overseas account and network. A Sentry account is also required.

items.name: Heptabase plugin for Claude / Claude Code
items.summary: After its ChatGPT and Codex plugins, Heptabase released a Claude plugin: search, view and edit your Heptabase notes and whiteboards from inside Claude.
items.howTo: Use the link in Heptabase's official post to add the plugin in Claude or Claude Code and authorize your account.
items.accessNote: Needs an overseas Claude account; Heptabase itself works in mainland China.

items.name: Autoharness: a Claude Code plugin that writes its own skills
items.summary: Learns skills from your real coding sessions, then automatically merges duplicates, updates them and cleans out unused ones, touching only the skills it created. MIT open source.
items.howTo: Install it in Claude Code with /plugin; see the link in the original post.
items.accessNote: GitHub usually opens and downloads fine from mainland China; using it with Claude Code needs an overseas account and network.

items.name: IdeaScientist research-workflow plugin
items.summary: IdeaScientist's research workflow rewritten as a Claude Code plugin: 4 skills and 7 agents that, with one command, search the literature, find gaps, propose ideas, argue against themselves and write a falsifiable research plan.
items.howTo: Install it into Claude Code from the link in the original post, then give it a research question.
items.accessNote: GitHub usually opens and downloads fine from mainland China; using it with Claude Code needs an overseas account and network.

items.name: Codex composer predictions (beta)
items.summary: Codex suggests the next message you're about to send, based on the conversation and how you usually write. Currently in beta for Pro users.
items.howTo: Pro users just chat in Codex as usual and will see predictions; accept or ignore them as prompted.
items.accessNote: OpenAI doesn't serve mainland China; you need an overseas Pro account and network.

items.name: New Codex sandbox on Windows (Microsoft MXC execution containers)
items.summary: Codex on Windows adds a sandbox mode built on Microsoft Execution Containers: faster install, stricter network limits and fine-grained control over file access.
items.howTo: Needs a compatible Windows 11 device; update Codex and pick the new sandbox mode in settings.
items.accessNote: Needs an overseas OpenAI account and network.

items.name: Cursor /visualize now takes follow-up questions in the same chat
items.summary: After /visualize draws a chart, you can keep asking in the same conversation and it will draw a new chart for each new question.
items.howTo: In the Cursor Agents window, type /visualize plus your question; once the chart appears, just keep asking.
items.accessNote: Cursor can be downloaded in mainland China, but some models are region-restricted; an overseas network is more reliable.

items.name: Copilot code review: org billing controls + review requests via API
items.summary: Organizations can now manage billing for Copilot code review separately, and new REST/GraphQL endpoints let you request a code review and set review effort per request. The default is now Balanced.
items.howTo: Org admins adjust billing in Copilot settings; developers call the API as documented in the changelog.
items.accessNote: GitHub and Copilot generally work directly in mainland China; paying requires an international credit card.

items.name: Ponytail 5 (DietrichGebert/ponytail)
items.summary: Makes your agent write the least code possible, like the laziest senior engineer. v5 rewrites the rules and adds /ponytail-review for full reviews and /ponytail-audit for whole-repo audits. The author's own test on 39 tasks showed 53% less code and 26% lower cost.
items.howTo: Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail, then /plugin install ponytail@ponytail. Codex has equivalent commands.
items.accessNote: GitHub usually opens and downloads fine from mainland China (sometimes slowly). It's used with coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, each of which needs its own account. The performance numbers are the author's own tests.

items.name: anthropics/skills official skills library
items.summary: Anthropic's official Agent Skills repo (about 180K stars), with Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF document skills plus example skills. On Oct 5 the claude-api skill was updated so it can bootstrap a Managed Agent from a quickstart name or URL.
items.howTo: In Claude Code, run /plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills, then install with /plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills.
items.accessNote: The repo usually opens and downloads fine from mainland China. The skills work in Claude Code and in other agents that support SKILL.md.

items.name: HTML plan skill for Claude Code (preview)
items.summary: Thariq from the Claude Code team is building a skill that has Claude write plans as HTML in plain language, with code snippets, a list of open questions and UI sketches, and uses linting to cut common mistakes.
items.howTo: Still gathering feedback and the post has no public install yet; follow the author for the official release.
items.accessNote: Once released it will also be used with Claude Code, which needs an overseas account and network.

items.name: Cursor: custom tools support MCP annotations and a replaceable system prompt
items.summary: Custom tools can now carry MCP annotations such as readOnlyHint and destructiveHint, so the model knows before calling whether it's a lookup or a delete. You can also swap in your own system prompt while rules, skills and tool definitions still load (rolling out by account).
items.howTo: Add the annotations in Cursor's MCP or custom tool config; put skills in .cursor/skills/ or .agents/skills/ and call them with /skill-name.
items.accessNote: Cursor can be downloaded and installed in mainland China, but calling overseas models usually needs a stable overseas network.

items.name: mattpocock/skills v1.3 (implement-spec)
items.summary: Engineering skills collection from TypeScript teacher Matt Pocock (about 280K stars). v1.3 makes implement-spec official: it breaks a whole spec into a task graph, has several sub-agents implement it in parallel in their own worktrees, then runs one combined code review.
items.sourceName: X · @0xGky “Top 4 on this period's Claude Code star chart”
items.howTo: Claude Code: claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official. Other agents: npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills.
items.accessNote: GitHub usually opens and downloads fine from mainland China (sometimes slowly). It's used with coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, each of which needs its own account.

items.name: Nylas email templates skill (nylas-email-templates)
items.summary: A new official skill from Nylas that teaches coding agents to build email automation end to end: write strict-mode Handlebars templates, test rendering, create workflows and debug mail that won't send. 20 sample templates were open-sourced too.
items.howTo: npx skills add nylas/skills --skill nylas-email-templates (works with 40+ agents including Claude Code, Cursor and Codex).
items.accessNote: The skill files install fine from mainland China, but Nylas is an overseas email and calendar API service that needs its own account.

items.name: addyosmani/agent-skills 0.6.12
items.summary: A production-grade engineering skills pack from Addy Osmani of the Chrome team: 25 skills covering requirements, planning, implementation, testing and shipping. The new version fixes the spec flow carrying on past the human sign-off step.
items.howTo: npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills (add --list to browse first, or --skill with a name to install just one).
items.accessNote: GitHub usually opens and downloads fine from mainland China (sometimes slowly). It's used with coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, each of which needs its own account.

items.name: Claude Code Mods
items.summary: Rewrite Claude Code's behavior and interface with a few lines of TypeScript: intercept or rewrite prompts and tool calls, add buttons and panels, replace built-in features. Mods ship inside plugins and work in both the CLI and the desktop app.
items.howTo: Type /plugin in the Claude Code CLI or desktop app to install a plugin that includes a mod, or just ask Claude to write one and hot-reload it.
items.accessNote: Anthropic doesn't serve mainland China; you need an overseas account and network. Mods aren't sandboxed, so only install ones from trusted sources.

items.name: Perplexity Computer × Amex business skills library
items.summary: Perplexity Computer added a set of ready-made skills curated by Amex, covering everyday small-business work such as cash-flow forecasting and marketing campaign generation. Pick a task, fill in your business details and run it.
items.howTo: Eligible US Amex business card members link their card, then choose the skill in Computer.
items.accessNote: Only for eligible US Amex Small Business card members; not available to users in mainland China.

items.name: obra/superpowers v6.4.2
items.summary: A skills framework with about 297K stars that forces agents through an engineering process: brainstorm, write a plan, write tests first, then code, then review. The new writing-plans step produces leaner plans; the author says planning time drops to about a quarter.
items.howTo: In Claude Code, run /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official.
items.accessNote: GitHub usually opens and downloads fine from mainland China (sometimes slowly). It's used with coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, each of which needs its own account.

items.name: Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills (community project)
items.summary: 817 cybersecurity skills across 29 areas including threat hunting, incident response, digital forensics and cloud security, mapped to frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK and NIST CSF 2.0. Note: this is a community project and has nothing to do with Anthropic.
items.howTo: npx skills add mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills.
items.accessNote: GitHub usually opens and downloads fine from mainland China (sometimes slowly). It's used with coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, each of which needs its own account. Scan it with SkillSpector before installing.

items.name: Gemini Skills launch worldwide, replacing Gems
items.summary: Save instructions you use often as skills in Gemini and call them up by typing /. You can stack several skills at once and attach reference files such as PDFs and images. Gems migrate to skills automatically.
items.howTo: Type / in the Gemini chat box to create or call a skill, or ask Gemini to turn an existing conversation into a skill.
items.accessNote: Gemini isn't offered in mainland China; you need an overseas Google account and network. Gems on personal accounts are phased out starting in November.

items.name: Workspace skills: SKILL.md compatible + rollout timeline
items.summary: Google confirmed that skills in Gemini and Workspace are based on the open SKILL.md standard, so skills written for other platforms can be copied over. Workspace started rolling out on Oct 5 and the Gemini app starts on Oct 13, finishing by mid-November.
items.howTo: Workspace users can create and share skills in the skill builder in Google Docs. Skills don't sync between the Gemini app and Workspace yet, so create them separately in each.
items.accessNote: Needs a Google Workspace Business or Enterprise license and an overseas network.

items.name: ChatGPT Plugin Extensions
items.summary: Announced at DevDay 2026: plugins can open apps in the ChatGPT sidebar, open panels beside the chat, and add file viewers/editors and forms. The UI ships bundled with the plugin's tools and skills.
items.howTo: Developers build and submit for review following the docs at developers.openai.com/plugins; users install from the ChatGPT plugin directory (@-mentions currently work only in the desktop app).
items.accessNote: OpenAI doesn't serve mainland China; you need an overseas account and network. OpenAI says web extensions for Free and Go are coming soon.
